text: Here's the scenario for this lab: an employee submits an Equipment Request containing several Requested Items — a laptop, a monitor, a headset. Once a manager approves the Request, items costing over one thousand dollars need an extra approval step from IT Asset Management, and every single approved item, regardless of cost, needs its own fulfillment task.

The flow triggers on Request Approved, which exposes pills for the Request record itself. A flow variable, extra underscore approval underscore threshold, is defined once at one thousand — a business rule value with no record behind it, which is exactly why it belongs in the Flow Variables panel rather than being pulled in as a pill.

A Look Up Records step pulls every Requested Item tied to that approved Request into one multi-record pill. A For Each loop iterates over that list, exposing a brand new current-item pill on every single pass through the loop, carrying that one item's own price and description.

Inside the loop, an If/Else compares the current item's price against the threshold flow variable, not a hard-coded number. Crossing the threshold routes that pass to an Ask for Approval action addressed to IT Asset Management. Staying at or under the threshold skips straight past approval instead.

Still inside the same loop, a Create Record action builds one fulfillment task on every single pass, regardless of which branch that item took. A Request with three Requested Items therefore produces exactly three fulfillment tasks — no hand-copied steps, and no logic retyped more than once.

One trigger, one flow variable, one list pill, one loop, one condition re-evaluated per item — that's the entire design, start to finish. Next up, Chapter Three begins with the built-in actions every flow relies on: Create, Update, and Notify.
